newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers deal seen unlikely in 48 hours.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers deal seen unlikely in 48 hours.

text.p: Federmeccanica, the Italian metalworkers employers' federation, said on Thursday the chance of a swift deal to end a bitter contracts dispute was slim.

"The possibility of reaching an accord in the next 48 hours is very remote," Federmeccanica head Michele Figurati told reporters after presenting his list of demands to Labour Minister Tiziano Treu. He did not give precise details.
"Treu didn't seem very impressed. He said he would examine it and reply," Figurati said.
He added a quick deal also seemed out of reach "because the position of the unions is just as rigid".

Figurati earlier described the situation as "terrible, very complicated, difficult" on his way into separate talks with Treu and metalworkers and engineering unions to try to end the months-long dispute.
Treu, who has been locked in talks with employers and unions all day, had said he hoped to be able to submit a proposal to metalworkers by Saturday to end the dispute over contracts.

Unions representing 1.7 million workers in the metalworking and engineering sector, which accounts for about 40 percent of total manufacturing output in Italy, are locked in dispute with management over pay increases for the 1996-1998 period.

Union leaders said earlier that Federmeccanica was talking tough. Figurati said his group's position was essentially that it wanted a commitment from the government to lower labour costs, with special additional measures for the poor south.
Union leaders told reporters that Federmeccanica was unimpressed with what the government was planning to offer.
Metalworkers' contracts expired in June and unions have recently held two national strikes in support of their claims for wage rises.
